@@ -78,7 +78,7 @@ The server exposes tools across three modules in `crates/app/src/mcp/` (see `cra
 - `set_wcs { "origin"?: [x, y, z], "stock_point"?: string, "offset"?: [dx, dy, dz], "rotation"?: [qx, qy, qz, qw] }`: Place the active setup's WCS origin and orientation quaternion.
 - `set_wcs_circle_centre { "edge": { "model": string, "id": "chain:0x…" }, "rotation"?: [qx, qy, qz, qw] }`: Place the active setup's WCS origin on the centre of a picked circular edge (a hole rim or boss edge, full circle or arc), at the edge's height; returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. Refuses a straight edge, a non-circular curve, a face or a vertex by name (#739).
 - `set_wcs_from_features { "picks": [{ "model": string, "id": string, "role": "origin" | "x" | "y" | "z" }], "setup"?: string }`: Place the active setup's WCS on a frame fitted to `list_features` picks - the GUI's "Set WCS from features" law (#701, #937). Axes read in Z, X, Y priority: the first axis pick is exact, the second squared to it, the third derived right-handed. A flat face sets its outward normal, a straight edge its direction, a curved wall (face or patch) its fitted axis; the origin is a vertex, a face's centroid or a wall's centre (else the second axis pick's anchor), projected onto the first pick's plane when that is a face. One undo step. Refused by name: under two picks, a role given twice, under two axes, a pick that cannot set its role, near-parallel axes (< 5 deg), a stale id, a `setup` that is not the active one. Note: a `list_features` face row's `normal` is the plane's canonical normal, not its outward side - tell faces apart by `bounds`.
-- `set_work_offset { "word": "G54" | "G55" | ... | "G59" | null, "setup"?: string }`: Set the posted G-code fixture coordinate word (G54–G59); `null` clears it.
+- `set_work_offset { "index": integer | "G54".."G59" | null, "word"?: (alias of index), "setup"?: string }`: Set the work offset a declared setup posts at (#931). `index` is 1-based, up to the maximum of the setup's own post (6 on most posts, 9 on Tormach PathPilot); the words `G54`–`G59` are accepted as aliases of 1–6, and `word` is the older spelling of the same argument (give one, or both agreeing). An offset the setup's post cannot express is refused by setup name (e.g. `setup Setup1 uses work offset 7, but its post ... expresses work offsets 1-6 only`). `null` clears it (offset 1). Returns `{ setup, index, name, word, label }`: `name` is what the post calls the offset (e.g. `G55`, `G59.1`, or `work offset 9` when the post gives none); `word` is kept as an alias of `name`. `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` and `set_wcs` carry the same `index` / `name` / `word`.
 - `load_machine { "builtin"?: string, "path"?: string, "clear"?: boolean, "setup"?: string }`: Mount a machine configuration at document or setup level: a built-in preset by name (`"VMC 3-axis"`, `"Lathe"`, the Tormach models, ...) or a `.mch` file by path; `clear: true` mounts none.
 - `set_workholding_max_rpm { "max_rpm": number | null, "setup"?: string }`: State the rated maximum rpm of a setup's chuck or collet; `null` clears it. Refused with a named error: a missing or non-numeric value, zero, negative or non-finite numbers, anything under 1 rpm or over 100000 rpm, an unknown setup, and a value the setup already states. `setup` defaults to the active one. One undo step. At post time, a constant-rpm (G97) turning operation faster than the limit is refused by name, and a constant-surface-speed (G96) section's rpm ceiling is capped at it (Fanuc `G50 S`, Tormach `G96 D`).
 - `edit_machine { "patch": object, "setup"?: string }`: Edit the mounted machine's definition with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396: an object merges, `null` removes a key, any other value replaces), e.g. `{"edm": {"max_orbit_radius": 0.5}}`. Keys are those `get_job`'s `machine.definition` shows. Applies as one undo step, like the Machine window's Apply. Refused by name, changing nothing: a `patch` that is not an object, an unknown key, an insane value, no machine mounted (`load_machine` first), an unknown setup, or a `setup` that follows the document's machine (edit that one, or give the setup its own first). Without `setup`, edits the document's machine.

+## #931 - work offsets as an index, the post supplies the word (slice 3: UI and MCP)
+
+**Decided.** The Setups page combo (also drawn on the WCS page) lists
+offsets `1..=max` of the setup's OWN post, read from
+`setup::work_offset_names` (the cached table from slice 2), each worded
+"Work offset n (NAME)", or "Work offset n" when the post gives that
+offset no name (the triage wording note). The wording lives in app
+(`setup_offsets::entry_label`) so the UI and any later caller share one
+spelling. The default post lists six entries; Tormach PathPilot lists
+nine (G59.1-G59.3).
+
+**A stored pick beyond the post's range stays visible as itself.** When a
+setup holds offset 9 and is switched to a six-offset post, the combo
+shows "Work offset 9 - not on this post" as the selected entry and lists
+it after 1-6 (and only it - offsets 7 and 8 are not offered, since the
+command would refuse them). The post gate from slice 2 refuses it by
+setup name. Considered and dropped: hiding it (the combo would read as
+offset 1 - the silent fallback triage point 2 forbids) and clamping it
+(a write the user did not ask for).
+
+**Other UI words.** Slice 2 already moved the browser tree, the heights
+page row, the viewport chips (`interact.rs`) and the status line
+(`state.rs`) to `setup::wcs_name`. Left here: the combo's hover text, the
+heights page hint and the WCS page's "Work offset:" line, which named a
+fixed "G54-G59" range; all three now say the post names the offsets
+(the WCS page line shows in a release-lane snapshot, regenerated at the
+cut; its structural twin `one_wcs` is updated here). The probe page's "Set G54".."Set G59" results
+are unchanged on purpose: the probe register arithmetic reaches offsets
+1-6 only (triage point 4), so a probe never sets an extended offset.
+
+**MCP.** `set_work_offset` takes `index` (1-based; a number, or the words
+G54-G59 as aliases of 1-6) and keeps `word` as the older spelling of the
+same argument. Both may be given only if they agree. Parsing
+(`setup_offsets::parse_index`) checks only the shape and the core sanity
+bound (1-255); whether the setup's post can express the offset is the
+command's check (`SetSetupWorkOffset::new` -> `setup_offsets::check`), so
+the MCP refusal is the GUI's refusal, by setup name. The reply, `set_wcs`
+and `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` carry `index` and `name`, with `word` kept
+as an alias of `name`. Considered and dropped: accepting a post's own
+name (e.g. "G59.1") as input - names are display only and differ by
+post, so the number is the one stable input.
+
+**PROCESS_VERSION** is bumped to 21 (the camcraft-mcp skill doc changed):
+one above the highest open bump (20, PR #1033). It renumbers at merge if
+another process PR lands first.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small: the wording is one function in app, the
+MCP aliases one parser.
